newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says ASEAN not interfering in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says ASEAN not interfering in Cambodia.

text.p: Thailand said on Friday that the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) was not interfering in Cambodia's internal affairs as it was meeting all key leaders involved in the country's political crisis.

Its remarks came as Cambodia's powerful premier Hun Sen shrugged off mounting international efforts to solve his country's political crisis and told foreigners, including ASEAN, to stay out of his affairs.

"We want to see peace reported in Cambodia as soon as possible. But we have no intention to interfere in the internal matters of Cambodia. We will use the Paris Agreement as our guideline in dealing with the issue," said Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn.

Prachuab and his counterparts from Indonesia, Ali Alatas, and Domingo Siazon from the Philippines are due to meet ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh in Bangkok at around 1100 GMT on Friday for talks on the political upheaval in Cambodia.
"(ASEAN's dialogue with Ranariddh) is within the framework of ASEAN's policy, not an interference," the minister said.

ASEAN was a co-signatory of the 1991 Paris accords which ended years of conflict and laid the grounds for U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993. Ranariddh was deposed on July 6 when Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's forces violently crushed Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC troops and drove them out of Phnom Penh earlier.

The foreign Ministers of Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, the Philippines, Vietnam and Brunei decided last week to postpone Phnom Penh's admission to ASEAN because of the political turmoil in Cambodia.
Cambodia had been due to join ASEAN in its 30th anniversary year together with Burma and Laos at next week's annual foreign ministerial conference in Kuala Lumpur.

ASEAN Secretary-General Ajit Singh said on Friday that Cambodia would still attend the group's foreign ministerial meeting next week as an observer with a delegation headed by Foreign Minister Ung Huot.

Singh told a Jakarta news conference: "All we know is that the observer delegation will be led by Mr Ung Huot", who was nominated earlier this week to replace ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
"The decision...to postpone the admission of Cambodia is in fact telling Cambodia that you cannot join ASEAN with a house divided," Singh said.
"Now put your house in order, and we in ASEAN are prepared to help you in any way that we can, or any way that you would like us to help you," Singh said.
He expressed confidence, however, that Cambodia would ultimately join the regional grouping.
"All three (Cambodia, Burma and Laos) qualify technically to join ASEAN -- it is only a question now of really timing."
The three foreign ministers, who met Cambodian King Norodom Sihanouk in Beijing on Thursday, were due to go to Phnom Penh for talks with Hun Sen.
Thailand's Prachuab said that after meeting Hun Sen the ministers would report back to the ASEAN ministerial meeting in Malaysia on July 23 and then decide on the future policy on Cambodia.
He said King Sihanouk wanted all Cambodians to adhere to the principles of the nation's constitution and he supported ASEAN's stance on the return of peace and unity to Cambodia.
Prachuab also told a news conference that Thailand would not allow itself to be used as a staging point for resistance against Hun Sen by those opposed to him.

"Thailand has no intention of any policy to support anybody to come here to use Thailand as a base of resistance by force," the minister said. "He (Ranariddh) has been informed of that and he has understood it very clearly."
Ranariddh would leave for Singapore on Sunday, he added.
